A batch of 4,096 examples supplies many inexpensive negatives, but two examples can share a valid meaning, entity, or label. Treating one as the other's negative creates a contradictory training signal. Deduplicate exact/near duplicates, mask known related items, or use a multi-positive target rather than blindly using the identity matrix as labels. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

One objective is $L_i=-\log\frac{\sum_{j\in P(i)}e^{s_{ij}/\tau}}{\sum_{j\in C(i)}e^{s_{ij}/\tau}}$, where positives and eligible candidates are explicit. This objective rewards total positive mass; averaging individual positive log probabilities has different behavior. Mine hard negatives only after checking relevance, and evaluate on independent labels. Larger batches improve candidate diversity but do not make every nonmatching row a true negative.
